catalogueCourses.recommendedPreparation: this course has no formal entry requirements, except valid enrollment. yet, it is indispensable to have sufficient knowledge of statistics and linear algebra. the reason for not demanding specific courses as formal entry requirements is to avoid excluding students who just did not pass one of the relevant preparatory courses. this course builds on a series of courses and uses the knowledge gained there. it is recommended that students have ready knowledge of: probability theory and statistics 1 probability theory and statistics 2 probability theory and statistics 3 * mathematics 2: linear algebra mathematics 3: advanced linear algebra introduction econometrics and actuarial science * *strongly advised for econometrics & data science/actuarial science students. this also holds for business analytics students (although the course does not belong to the mandatory program). for minor students requirements set by the program director must be met.

curriculum: The 2026–2027 UvA Business Analytics curriculum lists ten required 6 EC courses in each of the first two years. The final year is a 30 EC choice block, three compulsory 6 EC courses and two separate 6 EC thesis courses running in parallel. The English overview combines the thesis into one 12 EC bullet and omits a credit value in one table cell. The dated catalogue and Dutch study page agree on 6 EC each. The 12 EC internship is one option within the 30 EC group, with 18 EC remaining if chosen. No elective package or separate named route is selected. The catalogue narrative mentions first-year business law and ethics generically. The actual required list identifies AI, Privacy and Global Cybersecurity, with legal and ethical topics in that course, so there is no extra course.
progression: The standard curriculum completes all 60 EC in year one, meeting the published 48 EC binding study advice threshold, and reaches 120 EC before year three. This satisfies the 90 EC prerequisite for the optional internship and the 120 EC threshold for both thesis courses. For a company thesis project, Research Project states the 120 EC deadline of 1 March 2027. The choice remains open. Calculus precedes probability, and probability 1 precedes probability 2. Both probability courses and introductory linear algebra precede introductory data science. Calculus and linear algebra precede advanced linear algebra. Probability, linear algebra and advanced linear algebra precede Econometrics 1. That course recommends additional preparation shared with other degrees without requiring it for enrolment here. Programming, data structures and machine learning precede Language Technologies and Models. The research course leads to an individual thesis and prototype, with the companion Skills course teaching design science, project management and responsible AI deployment.
